title: Degree of unsaturation
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-02T04:41:50Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches how iodine absorption measures the number of carbon-carbon double bonds in a fat or oil: the carbon-13 NMR card is about counting carbon environments, and the alkanes, alkenes and alkynes card only introduces unsaturation as a family definition, which is related but not the same idea.

draft.title: Degree of unsaturation
card: Fats and oils are made of long hydrocarbon chains. Some chains have C=C double bonds. The more double bonds, the more unsaturated the fat or oil.
Iodine adds across a C=C double bond. One iodine molecule (I2) reacts with each double bond.
The iodine number is the mass of iodine, in grams, absorbed by 100 g of fat or oil. A higher iodine number means more double bonds.
To compare samples, use the same mass of each. The sample that absorbs more iodine has more C=C bonds.
draft.remember: More iodine absorbed means more C=C double bonds, so a higher degree of unsaturation.

a.q: Which fat or oil is the most unsaturated?
opts: The one with an iodine number of 130
The one with an iodine number of 90
The one with an iodine number of 50
The one with an iodine number of 10
a.why: A higher iodine number means more iodine was absorbed, so there are more C=C double bonds. A low number such as 10 shows few double bonds, so that fat is more saturated.

b.q: Tom tests 100 g samples of oil P, Q and R. They absorb 15 g, 85 g and 60 g of iodine. Which statement is correct?
opts: Q has more C=C bonds than R
P has more C=C bonds than Q
R has more C=C bonds than Q
P has more C=C bonds than R
b.why: Equal masses were used, so the sample that absorbed more iodine has more double bonds. Q absorbed 85 g and R absorbed 60 g, so Q has more C=C bonds than R.
b.clue: Rank the samples by iodine absorbed.

a.best: The one with an iodine number of 130

b.best: Q has more C=C bonds than R

problems.detail: "Fats and oils are made of long hydrocarbon chains" oversimplifies. Fats and oils are triglycerides: esters of glycerol with fatty acids, which contain long hydrocarbon chains. Year 12 students should not come away thinking fats are hydrocarbons.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer (130; Q has more C=C bonds than R), and the explanations match. One small issue: the card describes fats and oils as made of hydrocarbon chains when they are triglycerides (esters) containing hydrocarbon chains.

proposal.title: Degree of unsaturation
card: Fats and oils are triglycerides: esters of glycerol and three fatty acids. Each fatty acid has a long hydrocarbon chain.
Some of these chains contain C=C double bonds. The more double bonds, the more unsaturated the fat or oil.
Iodine (I2) adds across a C=C double bond, one I2 molecule for each double bond. So the amount of iodine absorbed shows how many double bonds there are.
The iodine number is the mass of iodine, in grams, absorbed by 100 g of fat or oil. With equal masses, the sample that absorbs more iodine has more C=C bonds.
proposal.remember: More iodine absorbed means more C=C double bonds, so a higher degree of unsaturation.

opts: The one with an iodine number of 130

b.q: Tom tests 100 g samples of oil P, Q and R. They absorb 15 g, 85 g and 60 g of iodine. Which statement is correct?
opts: Q has more C=C bonds than R
P has more C=C bonds than Q
